scores.claim_text: In the United States, Waystar has obtained 15 issued patents (plus 26 trademark and 26 copyright registrations).
scores.M_check: uspto_odp.query_assignee on parent name and acquired-entity name variants (Waystar, Waystar Technologies, Navicure, ZirMed, Recondo, eSolutions, Patientco)
scores.M_value: Waystar/Waystar Technologies: 0 applications (parent holds little IP under its own name). Acquired entities: ZirMed 6 applications / 1 granted; Navicure 9 applications; Recondo 2; eSolutions 4. USPTO indexes on firstApplicantName so an exact reconciliation to '15' is not possible, but a real, modest patent portfolio is confirmed across the named acquisition targets.
scores.interpretation: Waystar was assembled from nine acquisitions, so IP sits under acquired-entity names rather than the holdco. The claim is a modest, honest count (15 issued patents) and is directionally corroborated by granted/pending USPTO records across those entities. This is the opposite of the Nikola pattern (large patent claim, ~0 in the claimed area). PASS.

scores.claim_text: Following a recent cybersecurity incident involving one of Waystar's competitors, more than 30,000 providers began adopting Waystar's solutions, most signing two-to-three-year contracts.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext('Waystar') across all SEC filers; claim_evolution (IPO-date-bounded, no forward window).
scores.M_value: 124 total EDGAR full-text hits for 'Waystar' across filers (incl. healthcare names Oak Street Health, Enhabit, EngageSmart) — confirms a real, widely-referenced healthcare-payments vendor. No registry counts provider-adoption surges; the specific >30,000-provider figure is a self-asserted operational metric. claim_evolution window is empty by construction at the IPO cutoff (firewalled).
scores.interpretation: The competitor cyber incident is real and the broad ecosystem presence is corroborated, but the magnitude of the post-incident win (>30,000 providers, 48-hour implementations, new direct national-payer connectivity) is not in any federal/public registry. The disclosure is honestly framed ('began adopting', disclosed contract terms). Per Heuristic 8, SaaS adoption counts are not registry-verifiable. UNVERIFIABLE (no manufactured severity).

scores.claim_text: Waystar serves ~30,000 clients / ~1 million distinct providers, including 18 of the top 22 U.S. News Best Hospitals.
scores.M_value: 124 all-filer hits confirm Waystar is named in numerous third-party SEC filings, including healthcare providers — consistent with a large, real client base. No registry enumerates which named hospitals are clients; the 'top 22 Best Hospitals' roster is a curated marketing claim with no counterparty-disclosure hook.
scores.interpretation: Real ecosystem presence is corroborated, but the specific named-customer roster (18 of top 22) and aggregate client/provider counts are not independently verifiable in any federal registry, and individual hospital clients do not separately disclose vendor relationships. Per Heuristics 5 and 8, these B2B relationships are not buyer-disclosed. UNVERIFIABLE.

scores.claim_text: In 2023 Waystar facilitated over five billion healthcare payment transactions worth over $1.2 trillion in annual gross claims volume, spanning ~50% of U.S. patients.
scores.M_check: No registry covers SaaS transaction throughput / gross claims volume (Heuristic 1: sector-registry match; Heuristic 8: SaaS metrics not in any federal registry).
scores.M_value: No applicable M-source. EPA/USAspending/USPTO/ClinicalTrials/openFDA/FDIC do not record healthcare-claims-clearinghouse transaction volume.
scores.interpretation: Transaction-count and gross-claims-volume metrics for a healthcare-payments clearinghouse are internal operating statistics with no independent public registry. Honestly scored UNVERIFIABLE rather than forcing a weak query.

scores.claim_text: Waystar was recently named the exclusive payments vendor for a leading national ambulatory EHR provider.
scores.M_check: Counterparty deliberately unnamed in the filing; no registry hook (Heuristic 5 counterparty-disclosure threshold cannot be applied without a named entity).
scores.M_value: No applicable M-source — the EHR provider is described generically ('a leading national ambulatory EHR provider') so no specific counterparty filing can be queried.
scores.interpretation: Exclusive-vendor partnership claims naming no specific counterparty cannot be tested against any registry. Not a contradiction; simply untestable. UNVERIFIABLE.

scores.claim_text: Waystar maintains a Receivables Facility with PNC Bank, N.A. as administrative agent under a receivables financing agreement dated August 13, 2021.
scores.M_value: 0 mentions of 'Waystar' in PNC Financial Services Group's own SEC filings. A bank that is administrative agent on a private borrower's receivables facility would not separately name that borrower in its 10-K, so absence is expected and non-informative (Heuristic 5: many real B2B relationships are not separately disclosed by the counterparty).
scores.interpretation: The facility is a hard-documented, dated credit agreement disclosed in the prospectus (defined term, dated 2021-08-13). PNC's non-disclosure of a single private-borrower facility is the expected baseline, not a contradiction. No independent registry corroborates beyond the filing itself. UNVERIFIABLE (not SEVERE — Heuristic 5 threshold not met).

scores.claim_text: Waystar's FY2023 statements carry a KPMG LLP unqualified opinion (auditor since 2021) with no going-concern doubt; FY23 revenue $791.0M, income from operations $142.1M.
scores.M_value: going_concern: signal=NO_GOING_CONCERN (0 matches). auditor_change: signal=CLEAN_AUDITOR_TENURE (0 Item-4.01 8-Ks, 0 Big-4 resignations, 0 disagreements). Prospectus shows KPMG unqualified opinion since 2021 and positive FY23 operating income (+$142.1M on $791.0M revenue).
scores.interpretation: Audit relationship is clean (Big 4, stable tenure, no disagreements/resignations) and there is no going-concern flag. The business is operationally profitable at the operating line (the net loss is driven by ~$2.2B LBO debt interest, fully disclosed). The financial-quality signals corroborate the prospectus's clean-audit framing. PASS.
